item.title: Re: Extended log?
item.content:encoded:
Understood, thanks.

As for asking the author… the real big question is whether Mr. Deeds can teleport within the Foundation universe, and how much matter he can take with him in the teleport. In the task involving the assassination of a D-class, it is not exactly clear whether he teleported or merely picked the lock in the door.

It is clear he can not teleport massive items like a Corvette convertible; there probably are Corvettes in unobserved hobbyist garages. The refusal to bring a Faberge egg might mean he can't teleport objects at all; on the other hand, perhaps all Faberge eggs are in locations observed by security cameras of the type Mr. Deeds can not disable. This would render him unable to teleport out of there.

The Usama Bin Laden case might mean he can not teleport, but the refusal was worded like this: "perhaps someone closer and less heavily guarded?". The "heavily guarded" part might simply mean that no unobserved spot was available close enough to bin Laden, while if a further spot were used, the butler would be killed before reaching his target. The "closer" part might mean that the teleportation is limited in distance.

This is quite an important matter because a way to teleport items, even limited in size/mass, in distance, and also requiring unobserved points of entry and exit, would be quite useful in the operation of Foundation mobile task forces.

I have a set of experiments that would ascertain his abilities, but I would have to assume the results, which might not be what the original author of the SCP intended. I will try the PM system once I have a fair draft with my assumptions in it.

P.S. Another observation is that Mr. Deeds' practical methodology might be somewhat limited. He can model complicated actions, as seen from his entry in Experiment Log T-98816-OC108/682. However, he did not model the solution to the Corvette request that he obviously does have. Namely, bring the appropriate amount of gold, exchange it at a bank or perhaps a shady pawn shop (which requires a large discount but won't try to trace the origin) for British pounds or other currency, and acquire the car by non-anomalous means.

item.title: Establishing some parameters
item.content:encoded:
Pursuant to some discussions on IRC, I think it's a good idea to start figuring out what Deeds can and can't do, and why.

I propose that everything Deeds does in response to a request is either a chore or an errand (or sometimes a combination of the two).

A chore is something that he can do without leaving the premises: answer these questions, clean my car, do my laundry, cut my hair, pose for a picture, kill that D-class, play Monopoly with me, sacrifice yourself to SCP-682, etc. Deeds can perform any chore that a human male is capable of performing. There's some stuff, like "bring me a human flesh sandwich" or "I'm thirsty, bring me a goblet of human blood", which is simply Not Done; however, I'm sure that he'd bring you human flesh and blood if the request wasn't phrased in a way that implied cannibalism.

An errand is something that requires that he go somewhere else. Deeds is able to complete an errand if a) it is something that can be performed by a human, and b) if it can be done without him being observed.

There are enough grenades that one could go missing; this is not the case for unique works of art like Faberge eggs, or hyper-regulated WMDs like man-portable nukes. If you want a brick of gold without anyone noticing that you took it, you'll have to salvage it from wreckage somewhere, and that means some sacrifices in terms of purity.

Deeds has ordinary human strength and can't carry a car around, so if he were to get one for you, he'd have to drive it, which would probably get noticed — especially if you're asking for such a specific car that he'd have to steal it from someone who'd notice. Same with asking Deeds to bring you another SCP: the Foundation would damn well notice that containment had just been breached.

The problem with assassinating bin-Laden was that, at the moment the request was made, bin-Laden was in a room full of people; it would have been impossible for Deeds to assassinate him right then without being noticed. Note that Deeds said it could not be done "at this time".

Deeds also has some sort of self-transport ability, which also applies to anything that he's able to carry. And he's got an expanded awareness that gives him whatever knowledge is necessary to complete an errand — or to know that it's not something he's capable of. This includes "where to stand in order to not be seen by any surveillance systems while he uses his self-transport ability", and — if need be — "how to induce a spontaneous temporary mechanical failure in all surveillance systems so that he can use his self-transport ability". He could do that right away, instead of searching for a place to not be seen; however, surveillance systems presumably belong to someone, and it would be inappropriate for him to tamper with them unless it was absolutely necessary.

He was able to kill the D-class in the next room because that was a chore, not an errand: getting the knife was an errand (which was done in the seconds that the cameras were off), but using it to kill the D-class didn't require anything anomalous except unthinking obedience.

Plus there's the whole "he's killed, and then we look away and his corpse vanishes, and then the next time we ring the bell he's alive and ready to obey again" thing, but that's not really very interesting.
